The 40G port mode needs IOS XR 7.8.x or higher" data-port-modes-qsfp-dd="10, 40 and 100 Gigabit Ethernet on the cage - data sheet Table 2, "2 QSFP-DD ports capable of 10Gb, 40Gb, and 100Gb Ethernet" - plus 1x100G transponder mode with a 400G digital coherent module, per Table 19 of the configuration guide, which lists ASR-9902 ports 11 and 37 and marks the 400G and muxponder modes No" data-power-input-ac="200-240 VAC high line, 90-130 VAC low line, 50-60 Hz" data-power-input-dc="-48 VDC nominal, -40.5 to -72 VDC, 40 A max per module" data-power-supply-pids="PWR-1.6KW-AC, PWR-1.6KW-DC" data-power-redundancy="1+1" data-fixed-board-allocation-w="614 W allocated to 0/0 ASR-9902-LC in the install guide's show environment example; not a chassis total" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-air-filter="ASR-9902-FILTER, one serviceable filter on the front" data-operating-temp="5 to 40 C (41 to 104 F)" data-storage-temp="-40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F)" data-operating-humidity="10 to 85 percent" data-storage-humidity="5 to 95 percent" data-operating-altitude="0 to 4000 m" data-route-processor="A99-RP-F, two, redundant" data-switch-fabric="one integrated" data-rp-memory="SDRAM DDR4 32 GB" data-software="Cisco IOS XR 64-bit" data-ethernet="10-Gbps IEEE 802.3ae, 25-Gbps IEEE 802.3by and 802.3cc, 40/100-Gbps IEEE 802.3ba, 100GE PHY monitoring, IEEE 802.x flow control, full duplex, per-port byte and packet counters" data-macsec="all forty-eight ports" data-timing="2 x BITS RJ-45, ToD RJ-45, 10 MHz and 1 PPS SMB per RP, IEEE 1588 PTP telecom profiles and SyncE" data-console="RJ-45 serial on each RP" data-auxiliary="RJ-45 serial on each RP" data-mgmt-ethernet="2 x RJ-45 per RP" data-usb="1 x USB class A per RP" data-etsi="EN300 386, ETSI 300 019 Storage 1.1, Transportation 2.3, Stationary 3.1, EN55022, EN55024, EN50082-1/EN-61000-6-1" data-emc="FCC Class A, ICES 003 Class A, AS/NZS 3548 Class A, CISPR 22 (EN55022) Class A, VCCI Class A, BSMI Class A, IEC/EN 61000-3-2, IEC/EN 61000-3-3" data-railway="EN50121-4" data-eol="none-announced">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>
